cards.subject: Lordaeron's western woodland
lines: Orchards, farmsteads, a producing mine, a garrison on the lake island, and a graveyard beside the road.
Everything you interact with here is the ruin of something that had a job.

cards.subject: The Sepulcher
lines: It is not a town. It is a graveyard on the road that the Forsaken parked their caravans in and never left.
The trainers, the vendors and the flight master are all standing in a cemetery, using a crypt as a building.
Two flight paths, to Undercity and Tarren Mill. That is the network.

cards.subject: Read the map
lines: Malden's Orchard. Olsen's Farthing. Valgan's Field. The Ivar Patch. The Dead Field.
Every one of them is somebody's land, and not one of them has a somebody left in it.
Nothing in the zone ever explains who they were. The names are the only record.

cards.subject: The worgen here are not Gilneas's
cards.tag: In 1.12 there is no Gilneas story
lines: Arugal was an archmage of Dalaran. He summoned them out of Ur's research to fight the Scourge on the Kirin Tor's behalf, and they turned on everyone.
Genn Greymane asking him for help at the Wall is a 2010 comic and Cataclysm. Standing here, that story does not exist.
Every worgen in this forest is one mage's mistake, still walking around.

cards.subject: Son of Arugal
cards.tag: On the roads, not in the keep
lines: Silverpine is a ten to twenty zone. These are level 24 to 25 elites, and they wander it.
They were only lowered to level 20 in patch 2.3, and deleted from the game entirely in 4.0.3a.
Arugal's Gift is a five minute shadow curse. It is still ticking long after you stopped running.

cards.subject: Fenris Keep
lines: Before the Third War it was a thriving military outpost of the kingdom of Lordaeron.
Thule Ravenclaw took the island and the ferry landing with it, and put his Rot Hide gnolls in the fortress.
A royal garrison, a plagued gnoll pack and a living human necromancer — three owners deep on one small island.

cards.subject: Deep Elem Mine
lines: The name comes from "Deep Elem Blues", which is itself about Deep Ellum, a neighbourhood in Dallas.
Inside, the worgen pack is led by Grimson the Pale.
He was the mine's foreman. The man who ran the place is still in it, on all fours.

cards.subject: Ambermill
cards.tag: A lit town in a dead forest
lines: Halfway down the zone there is a working human village with a working mill, held by wizards of Dalaran under Archmage Ataeric.
The Forsaken's claim on this forest is disputed by them, and this is the shape the dispute takes.
For a Forsaken player it is often the first living human town they have ever seen, and it is a target.

cards.subject: Who you are actually fighting
lines: There is no Alliance hub in Silverpine. The opposition a leveller meets here is the Kirin Tor.
It is the one low zone where the mage order is the occupying force.
Read the mob names before you pull. They are all Dalaran.

cards.subject: The quiet
lines: Tall silver-barked pines over grassy knolls, dilapidated farmsteads, abandoned mines.
The wiki's own words for it: eerily silent, save for the occasional unnatural howling echoing among the trees.
The zone is designed to sound empty so that the howl lands.

cards.subject: Pyrewood Village
cards.tag: Nine in the evening, server time
lines: The villagers are human by day and Moonrage worgen by night. At 8:59 they are people. At 9:00 they are not.
They turn back at dawn.
It is one of the very few real day-night mechanics in the whole game, and it runs whether anybody is watching or not.

seed.body: Get to Pyrewood by 8:55pm server and just stand in the road. Do it once.

cards.subject: The Greymane Wall
lines: A colossal sealed wall with a gate in it. In here it never opens, and there is no Gilneas — the land behind it is not built.
It is the only place in the old world where you can walk up to a door the developers deliberately shut and stand at it.
It stays closed for six more years.
